# Results — Study 728 ("people drink more beer in recessions")

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Are beer stocks defensive /
counter-cyclical? We test the two tradable beer names — **Molson Coors (`TAP`)** and
**Boston Beer (`SAM`)** — against **`SPY`** on (1) downside beta, (2) recession-window
returns and (3) tradability. Prices are real (month-end Adj Close, yfinance); the NBER
recession windows are **hardcoded, cited** official dates. Offline & deterministic; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Beer names | `TAP` (Molson Coors, NYSE) · `SAM` (Boston Beer, NYSE) — month-end Adj Close via yfinance, cached under `_cache/` |
| Benchmark | `SPY` (SPDR S&P 500 ETF, month-end Adj Close, yfinance) |
| Adjustment | `auto_adjust=True` — splits **and** dividends folded in (*total-return-ish*; labelled as such, not price-only) |
| Recession windows | **NBER** official contractions: 2001-03→2001-11, 2007-12→2009-06, 2020-02→2020-04 — **hardcoded, cited** ([`docs/references.md`](references.md)); a dated set of facts, not a feed |
| As-of | 2026-06-30 (month-end; no partial-month bar) |
| Window | 1995-01 → 2026-06 (SPY/TAP: 377 monthly returns; SAM from its 1995-11 listing: 367) |

> **Survivorship, named on the Signal axis.** Both firms *survived* the entire window, and
> `SAM` in particular is a craft-beer **winner** whose listed life is a selected success.
> The bias points **for** the defensiveness/outperformance claim, so any positive result
> here is treated with extra suspicion — and none clears the bar anyway.

## Half 1 — full-sample risk/return (what "holding beer" actually did)

| series | CAGR | ann. vol | Sharpe | max drawdown |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **TAP** (Molson Coors) | **+7.32%** | 26.9% | 0.40 | −66.4% |
| **SAM** (Boston Beer) | **+6.52%** | 37.4% | 0.36 | **−85.4%** |
| SPY | **+11.12%** | 15.1% | **0.78** | −50.8% |

Both beer names **badly lagged** the index over 31 years, with a *worse* Sharpe; `SAM`
also had a *deeper* drawdown. `$1` invested in 1995 → **`$27.45`** (SPY) vs **`$9.19`**
(TAP) / **`$6.91`** (SAM): the "defensive" hold ended at roughly a **third** of the index.

## Half 2a — downside defensiveness (bull vs bear beta, split at SPY = 0)

| name | down-beta β⁻ | up-beta β⁺ | full beta | asymmetry (β⁻−β⁺) | defensive? |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|:--:|
| **TAP** | **0.60** | 0.70 | 0.64 | −0.10 | yes (weakly) |
| **SAM** | **0.87** | 0.79 | 0.68 | **+0.09** | **no** |

`TAP` is a mild textbook defensive (β⁻ < β⁺ < 1). `SAM` is the **opposite** — it loads
*more* on the market in down months than up months. Two beer stocks, two opposite answers:
not the signature of a "beer is defensive" law. And both full betas are **below 1** — these
are simply low-beta stocks, which is not the same as counter-cyclical.

## Half 2b — recession-window returns vs SPY (the direct counter-cyclical test)

Paired monthly excess `r_stock − r_SPY` over the union of NBER recession months (n = 31):

| name | mean monthly (stock) | vs SPY | excess | *t* | p | cum (stock vs SPY) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **TAP** | −1.44% | −1.70% | +0.25%/mo | **+0.14** | 0.891 | −48.1% vs −45.6% |
| **SAM** | +2.42% | −1.70% | +4.12%/mo | **+1.87** | 0.071 | +64.3% vs −45.6% |

**Neither clears the `\|t\| ≥ 2` bar.** And the per-recession breakdown (compounded %)
indicts the aggregate:

| recession | n | TAP | SAM | SPY |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2001 dot-com | 9 | −13.8% | **+40.8%** | −7.1% |
| 2008 GFC | 19 | −19.3% | **−10.8%** | −35.5% |
| 2020 COVID | 3 | −25.4% | **+30.9%** | −9.2% |

`TAP` fell **more** than SPY in 2 of 3 recessions (2001, 2020), winning only the GFC.
`SAM`'s aggregate edge is **two idiosyncratic craft-beer rallies** (2001, 2020) — and in
**2008, the deepest and most beer-relevant recession, `SAM` *fell* 10.8%**. An edge that
reverses in the recession that most tests the thesis is not a beer effect.

## Half 3 — CAPM alpha vs SPY (Newey-West, 6-lag)

| name | annualised α | beta | NW *t*(α) | p |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **TAP** | +3.25% | 0.64 | +0.71 | 0.480 |
| **SAM** | +5.91% | 0.68 | +0.84 | 0.403 |

Both point estimates are positive but **insignificant** (`|t| < 1`). Whatever the low beta
bought, it was not statistically distinguishable alpha.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

A deterministic stock with a *planted* asymmetric beta (β⁻ = 0.50 in down months, β⁺ = 1.00
in up months, seed 728): the bull/bear engine recovers **β⁻ ≈ 0.48 < β⁺ ≈ 0.77**,
`recovered_defensive = 1`. The detector sees genuine downside defensiveness when it exists,
so the messy, name-dependent null on the real beer tape is a **real null**, not a blind
harness.

## Tradability — the look-ahead that kills it

The NBER *declares* a recession long after it starts: the 2008 recession's Dec-2007 peak was
dated in **Dec-2008** (~12 months late) and the 2020 trough (Apr-2020) in **Jul-2021** (~15
months late). A "rotate into beer when the recession hits" rule therefore requires a time
machine — it is a **look-ahead**. And the *permanent* beer tilt (the only implementable
version) compounds at a large discount to SPY (above).

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** No leg clears `|t| ≥ 2` in the beer's favour: recession-window excess
  `t` = +0.14 (TAP) / +1.87 (SAM, and it's two idiosyncratic windows); CAPM α insignificant
  (NW `t` = +0.71 / +0.84). Downside defensiveness holds for only one of the two names, and
  weakly. The "beer is recession-proof" claim earns no statistical support here.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** NBER recession dating is ~12 months *ex-post* (a look-ahead), so
  the recession-conditional trade is un-implementable; the buy-and-hold version turned `$1`
  into `$9.19`/`$6.91` vs SPY's `$27.45` over 31 years, with deeper drawdowns.
- **Counter-cyclical? — BUSTED.** The only real effect is *low beta* (TAP β ≈ 0.64), which
  is not counter-cyclicality: TAP fell **more** than SPY in 2 of 3 recessions, and SAM's
  down-beta (0.87) *exceeds* its up-beta (0.79). Beer stocks fell in downturns like
  everything else — they are (at most) low-beta, not counter-cyclical.

> **Caveat (named, not buried).** The recession sample is tiny (3 recessions, 31 months),
> so the recession-window tests are low-power by construction — which is *itself* part of
> the finding: three recessions cannot certify a "recession-proof" law, and the one clear
> signal (a large SPY-beating wealth path) points the *other* way. Prices are real and
> total-return-ish; the NBER windows are cited official dates. Both limitations push the
> verdict toward humility, not toward a stronger claim.
